claims.text: GDACS's event report for Tropical Cyclone DOLPHIN-26 assesses an Orange alert level (medium humanitarian impact), episode 42, with a maximum wind speed of 269 km/h (Category 5), an event window of 27 July-6 August 2026, roughly 16.9 million people exposed to Category 1 or higher wind speeds, affected countries listed as the Marshall Islands, Japan and China, and high vulnerability flagged specifically for the Marshall Islands.

GDACS's episode report for the same storm confirms an Orange alert level, a maximum wind speed of 269 km/h (Category 5), and an event timeline of 27 July-6 August 2026, with the GDACS score of 1.5 reflecting the cyclone's significant potential impact based on wind speed, storm surge and rainfall projections from multiple meteorological models (JTWC, HWRF, GFS, ECMWF).

GDACS's event report for Tropical Cyclone DOLPHIN-26 (event id 1001297) now shows episode 45 (window 27 Jul-7 Aug 2026, report timestamped 7 August 2026 08:50 UTC), still an Orange alert with a peak intensity of 269 km/h (Category 5), with population exposed to Category 1+ winds now assessed at approximately 21.2 million across the Marshall Islands, Japan and China, up from about 16.9 million as of episode 42. No allowlisted source (GDACS, ReliefWeb, WHO) has yet published a confirmed death, injury or evacuation figure.

Re-checked 8 August 2026: GDACS's event report for DOLPHIN-26 now reads "Overall Orange Tropical Cyclone for DOLPHIN-26 in Marshall Islands, Japan, China from 27 Jul 2026 00:00 UTC to 08 Aug 2026 06:00 UTC" -- the event window now closes today. Population exposed to Category 1 or higher winds has fallen sharply to about 4 million, down from approximately 21.2 million as of the 7 August check, consistent with the storm moving past the most populous areas as it tracks toward a China landfall; peak intensity is still listed at 269 km/h (Category 5) as the storm's historical maximum. No allowlisted source (GDACS, ReliefWeb, WHO) has yet published a confirmed death, injury or evacuation figure, and no dissipation/closure statement has been published.

GDACS's event report for Tropical Cyclone DOLPHIN-26 now covers a window of 27 Jul 2026 00:00 UTC to 09 Aug 2026 06:00 UTC, still Overall Orange, with peak intensity unchanged at 269 km/h (Category 5) and about 11.2 million people exposed to Category 1 or higher winds across Marshall Islands, Japan and China.

Re-checked 10 August 2026: GDACS's event report for DOLPHIN-26 (episode 55) still shows an event window ending 09 Aug 2026 12:00 UTC -- unchanged from the prior day's cutoff, rather than extending to 10 August as it had in every previous daily check -- indicating GDACS is no longer advancing the active window as the storm has moved past the tracked region. Alert level remains Orange, peak intensity unchanged at 269 km/h (Category 5), and population exposure is now listed at about 14.1 million in Category 1-or-higher winds. No allowlisted source has published a confirmed death, injury or evacuation figure for this storm at any point in its lifecycle.

description: Tropical Cyclone DOLPHIN-26 intensified to Category 5 strength (269 km/h sustained winds) in the western Pacific in late July 2026, tracking across the Marshall Islands and toward Japan's Ryukyu Islands (Okinawa Prefecture and the Daito Islands) and China. GDACS assessed the storm at an Orange alert level (medium humanitarian impact) throughout, with population exposure to Category 1 or higher winds peaking at approximately 21.2 million people and the Marshall Islands flagged for high vulnerability. By 10 August 2026 GDACS's event window had stopped advancing, remaining fixed at 9 August, indicating the storm had moved past the tracked region; the event is assessed as contained on that basis. No confirmed death, injury or evacuation figure was published by an authoritative source at any point in the storm's lifecycle.

impact.summary: GDACS assessed Tropical Cyclone DOLPHIN-26 at an Orange alert (medium humanitarian impact) with a peak intensity of 269 km/h (Category 5) across the Marshall Islands, Japan and China. Population exposed to Category 1 or higher winds peaked at approximately 21.2 million during the storm's active phase and stood at about 14.1 million in the final assessment, with the event window closed as of 9 August 2026 and the storm assessed as contained. No confirmed death, injury or evacuation figure was published by an authoritative source for this storm.

location.region: Western Pacific track across the Marshall Islands to the Ryukyu Islands (Okinawa, Daito Islands), Japan, and onward toward China

name: Super Typhoon Dolphin — Marshall Islands, Japan & China

updates.text: GDACS's event window stopped advancing day-over-day, remaining fixed at 12:00 UTC on 9 August 2026 — the signal that the storm had moved past the tracked region. The alert level remained Orange with population exposure listed at about 14.1 million, and the event status was updated to contained.

GDACS extended the event window to 9 August 2026, still at Orange alert, with peak intensity unchanged at 269 km/h and about 11.2 million people exposed to Category 1 or higher winds as the storm tracked toward the China coast.

Population exposed to Category 1 or higher winds fell sharply to about 4 million, from approximately 21.2 million the previous day, consistent with the storm moving past the most populous areas as it tracked toward a China landfall.

GDACS's episode 45 assessment raised population exposed to Category 1 or higher winds to approximately 21.2 million across the Marshall Islands, Japan and China, up from about 16.9 million, with peak intensity still 269 km/h (Category 5).
